title: An Agent-Based Model of Gonorrhea Transmission Applied to Evaluation of Performance of Different Surveillance Strategies for Antimicrobial-Resistant Gonorrhea
content: Purpose: To evaluate performance of different surveillance strategies for antimicrobial-resistant (AMR) gonorrhea. This can provide insights for different surveillance projects such as the Combatting Antimicrobial Resistant Gonorrhea and Other Sexually Transmitted Infections (CARGOS) etc. Methods: We developed an agent-based model of gonorrhea transmission among US men who have sex with men and calibrated it to local epidemiological data using the Bayesian calibration approach. The model also integrated a surveillance system for AMR gonorrhea, a feature that was not previously employed in any model of this kind.  Results: The absolute error of the strategy that utilizes isolates from symptomatic men with urethral gonorrhea is 2.6 (95% uncertainty interval (UI): 0, 6) years. In comparison, the absolute error of a lower-volume strategy that relies on a mix of urethral, rectal and pharyngeal isolates is 0.3 (95% UI: 0, 3) years. The exclusion of rectal isolates from this strategy would increase the estimation error to 0.9 (95% UI: 0, 4) years. This difference is statistically significant (sign test, p-value<0.01). Meanwhile, a significant increase in the number of urethral isolates used in the first strategy is not expected to improve the performance.  Conclusion: Extragenital isolates are important for the accurate surveillance of AMR gonorrhea and should be included in national surveillance strategies. The presented evidence supports the compulsory incorporation of rectal isolates in the CARGOS.
